title: IterNet: Retinal Image Segmentation Utilizing Structural Redundancy in Vessel Networks
mechanism: A shared-weight mini-UNet is applied repeatedly to the segmentation output itself (with skip connections from earlier iterations), with supervision at each iteration, so the network learns to complete broken thin structures.
evidence: R: DRIVE AUC 0.9816, CHASE-DB1 0.9851, STARE 0.9881; trained from 10 to 20 labelled images, no pretraining.
adaptation: Bolt 3 shared-weight mini-UNets onto the U-Net++ full-resolution output; each takes [1-ch EL, softmax of crack / inactive / gridline / splice, last decoder features]; house loss (CE + Dice on crack and inactive) on every iteration; end to end, no OOF data needed. Gridline (recall 0.33) is a periodic thin line and is a second target.
min_experiment: Arm: U-Net++ + 3-iteration IterNet head, 5 seeds, 20k steps. Baseline: house 5-seed (and PF variant if adopted). Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, gridline IoU and recall, mIoU_rob. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012 and relF1@2 < +0.01 and gridline IoU < +0.03.
prior_overlap: none. No iterative or stacked head was run; architecture changes tried were ResNet-50 encoder and 2x input only.

alt_notes.adaptation: Append 3 weight-shared mini-U-Nets after U-Net++ that read the softmax output (and last decoder features); loss CE + crack/inactive Dice at each stage; same label-safe augmentation, 20k steps; test on house and PF fine-tunes.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: U-Net++ + 3 IterNet stages, 5 seeds. Baseline: house and PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: clean-49 and 5-fold CV crack IoU, relF1@2, components found, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: crack IoU < +0.012 and no relF1@2 gain.
